title: Ganesha's song comes first
hookLine: the harmonium is ready, the room is full, and the first song goes to the god of beginnings
carry: honor Ganesha first: he clears the road
tomorrow: what does Om Namah Shivaya actually mean?

lines: A RUG, A HARMONIUM, A DRUM.
THE FIRST SONG GOES TO GANESHA.
cards: A rug on the floor, a harmonium in the middle of it, hand cymbals beside a drum. People drift in and sit cross-legged. Some know every word.
Some have never been to a kirtan and are already worried about singing badly.

The leader presses a key, the drone begins, and before any song to Krishna or Shiva, the first line goes out to someone else: an elephant-headed god, with a broken tusk and a sweet in one hand. The room sings it back.

teach.h: KIRTAN: NAMES SUNG BACK AND FORTH.
teach.b: Kirtan is singing the names and glories of God together, often as call and response: the leader sings a line, the room sings it back.

teach.h: A REPERTOIRE: SONGS KNOWN BY HEART.
teach.b: A repertoire is the songs a group knows by heart, the ones that can start without a songbook. For the next few days we'll build one, a song at a time, in roughly the order an evening might run.
Some halls begin with Ganesha. Tradition honors him first before many beginnings: a wedding, a new house, a school year, a puja.
He is called the remover of obstacles, and also their lord, the one who can place a block in the road or lift it. Tradition tells more than one story of why he goes first.
In one, from the Shiva Purana, Shiva restores the boy to life with an elephant's head after a terrible quarrel, and declares that he will be worshipped before every other god.

A Hindi aarti to him begins: Jai Ganesha, Jai Ganesha, Jai Ganesha Deva. Victory to Ganesha, victory to the god. The next line names his family: his mother is Parvati, his father is Mahadeva, the great god, Shiva.
So the first song is partly a family introduction. And the evening doesn't begin with the hardest song.
It begins by clearing the road. The nervous newcomer gets a simple line, sung slowly, and by the third round, it's in the room. In a kirtan, the first obstacle can be as small as opening your mouth.

how: At a kirtan a leader often sings a line and the group sings it back, with harmonium, drum and hand cymbals; some groups open the evening with a song to Ganesha, who is honored before beginnings.

games.q: you're leading a kirtan for the first time. the drone is going and the room is waiting. what's your first song?
o: a song to Ganesha, slow and simple.
the hardest song you know, to impress them.

games.why: some halls begin with Ganesha, honored before beginnings. a slow, simple line clears the road for nervous voices too.

practice: Let the shoulders drop and name one thing you're about to begin, a conversation, a piece of work, a trip, and then one thing that might block it: tiredness, worry, a person, a habit.

Don't try to solve it; just see the obstacle clearly and set it down in front of you. If you pray, say Ganesha's name once, softly, as some Hindus do before a beginning; if not, simply rest with the road in front of you.
